summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma and a history of biliary drains, was readmitted with nausea, chills, and absence of biliary drain output. He was initially treated with IV meropenem for suspected cholangitis. A cholangiogram revealed obstruction of the distal PTBD catheter, which was successfully replaced percutaneously. Post-procedure, his symptoms resolved, liver enzymes improved, and blood cultures remained negative. Infectious disease determined antibiotics were unnecessary, as the presentation was consistent with mechanical obstruction rather than infection. The drain was capped without complications, and he was discharged home with home health support for drain care. His thrombocytopenia remained stable, and oncology follow-up was arranged.
